definition: Engender means to give rise to a feeling, bond, or condition.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word engender. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know engender should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Nothing engenders loyalty in a kitchen crew like a chef who scrubs pots beside them on the worst nights.
Invite merely leaves the door open — conditions that invite gossip stop short of engendering it.
Ignite goes further than engender — what engender raises gradually, ignite sets blazing all at once.

To spark something is to set it off in an instant — one match dropped in dry grass, and the blaze is suddenly alive. Engender works at the speed of a season: what a policy engenders — trust, resentment, hope — gathers gradually in people rather than detonating.

To breed a feeling is to produce it steadily over long stretches of time, the way neglect breeds mistrust in a workplace. Engender is quicker and more bookish, but both are growth words: something engendered still takes root in people rather than appearing in an instant.

Engender means to give rise to a feeling, bond, or condition.

When the false rumor of a bank failure reached the market town, it engendered a panic no official denial could catch: by dawn a silent queue wrapped the square, and by noon the tellers' drawers were empty.
Engender is for what grows in people — trust, resentment, hope, panic — brought into being by something that happened.
You cause a delay and create a product, but you engender a feeling or a climate; the word remembers its root: to beget, to bring to birth.
Engender belongs in analysis — editorials, histories, board reports — wherever one thing gives rise to a mood or condition: reforms engender trust, shortages engender resentment.
For concrete outcomes use cause or produce; for a sudden flare, spark.
If nothing is growing in anyone, engender is the wrong tool.

She simply arrived early, learned every player's name in a week, and stayed late to help the cellists haul their cases to the bus stop.
